about: Flags for tools/build_flags.py. 'flags': rows that replace whatever Wikidata gives for a state in a span of years (file = Wikimedia Commons file name; flags: u = uncertain or not an official national flag, s = a royal banner or standard rather than a national flag; note is shown in the panel). 'drop': spans in which a state shows no flag although Wikidata gives one, each with the reason. 'checked': states whose undated Wikidata flag was read and holds for all the years the state is on the map. 'early': states whose flags before 1600 were read and are kept (other pre-1600 flags are dropped: most are modern drawings of arms or reconstructions). 'qid': map names that have no item in data/entities.json. 'standard': states whose flag in the given years is a royal banner or standard, not a national flag (also any file whose name says royal, standard or banner). 'modern': power keys whose present-day country (for the fill colour) is set by hand instead of measured from the maps. 'colors': present-day flag colours set by hand (first: the fill; second: the neighbour fallback). 'same_design': a file Commons would not serve to the build, and a file of the same design (a shade or proportion apart) shown in its place.

Russian Empire.note: The black-yellow-white imperial flag, approved by Alexander II in 1858.
White-blue-red: decreed for festive use by Alexander III in 1883 and made the national flag in 1896; the black-yellow-white flag stayed in some official use until then.

Austria-Hungary.note: Civil ensign. Austria-Hungary had no common national flag; Austria and Hungary each kept their own.

Austrian Empire.note: The black and yellow flag of the Austrian Empire.

Bourbon Kingdom of France.note: The white flag of the Bourbon Restoration.
The July Monarchy restored the tricolour in 1830.

Kingdom of Denmark.note: The Dannebrog, first shown as Denmark's in the Gelre Armorial (c. 1370 to 1386).

Confederate States of America.note: The 'Stars and Bars' with 13 stars (November 1861 to May 1863).

China.note: Qing dynasty: the triangular Yellow Dragon flag.
Qing dynasty: the rectangular Yellow Dragon flag.
Republic of China: the Five-Coloured Flag of the Beiyang government.

China.file: Flag of the Republic of China.svg
China.note: Republic of China: Blue Sky, White Sun, and a Wholly Red Earth (national flag from December 1928).

China.file: Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg
China.note: People's Republic of China: the Five-starred Red Flag (from 1 October 1949).

Persia.note: Lion and Sun tricolour of the Qajar and early Pahlavi state.

Iran.note: Provisional flag of the Islamic Republic, used until July 1980.
Flag of the Islamic Republic (from 29 July 1980).

French First Republic.note: The first tricolour, red at the hoist (1790 to 1794).
The tricolour as decreed on 15 February 1794.

Holy Roman Empire.file: Banner of the Holy Roman Emperor with haloes (1430-1806).svg
Holy Roman Empire.note: The imperial banner (double-headed eagle), the emperor's, not a national flag.

Habsburg Monarchy: No flag of the monarchy as a whole: the red-white-red Wikidata gives is the Austrian archduchy's banner, and the black and yellow imperial colours became a state flag only with the Austrian Empire (1804).
Holy Roman Empire Minor States: A grouping of the source map, not a state.
Tsardom of Russia: No national flag: the 1668 ship flag Wikidata gives is a reconstruction.
Mozambique: A Portuguese colony: Wikidata dates the 1983 flag wrongly.
Martinique: Wikidata gives the flag adopted in 2023.
Puerto Rico: The Puerto Rican flag was made official only in 1952 (a Spanish, then US territory).
Venezuela: Wikidata's dates for Venezuela's 19th-century flags do not match the flags' own years.
Cuba: A Spanish colony, then under US military rule, until 1902.
Jammu and Kashmir: Wikidata gives the state flag of 1952.
Taiwan: A Japanese colony until 1945 (no flag of its own), then a province of the Republic of China.
Korea: Not checked: Joseon and the Korean Empire used the Taegeukgi from 1883, Korea was Japanese from 1910.

checked.Kingdom of France: The royal standard (white with gold fleurs-de-lis); the kingdom had no national flag.
checked.Dutch Republic: The States Flag (red-white-blue), the republic's flag from the mid-17th century; the Prince's Flag (orange-white-blue) was used before.

early.Kingdom of England: The royal banner of the arms (from c. 1200) and St George's cross.
early.Kingdom of Portugal: The royal banners of the arms, which changed with the arms.
early.Spanish Empire: The Cross of Burgundy, the Spanish military and naval flag from 1506.
early.Republic of Pisa: The red flag with the white cross of Pisa.
